title: Canal Boatman
premise: A long master-and-apprentice drama at the stone barge boathouse and Third Lock. Ashu and Asheng are easily confused by looks; the elm tiller goes intact→split→banded repaired; after Qingque hits the lock and sinks it must be avoided; count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.
_comment: Author layer: humans only write entities + state machines + per-scene timelines (present + handwritten action + semantic events). present items may be objects carrying confusable_with/count/anchor metadata. op/gap/probe/forbidden are derived by complete_gt.py.
_state_note: Entities with state machines use states; entities without use appearance. On transition inject only the current-state look.

states.prime_steersman: Canal boatman Wei Ran in his forties, sun-reddened face, indigo short jacket and woven-straw sandals, bamboo water gauge at the waist, steady stride.
states.damp_weary: The same Wei Ran: jacket soaked clinging, right knee wrapped in wet cloth, walking slowly on a bamboo pole, eyes heavy.
states.deceased: Wei Ran has closed his eyes in death, lying still on the boathouse plank bed, face peaceful, no breath left.

states.young_apprentice: Young Ashu: a lean boatwright apprentice of fourteen or fifteen, a celadon water-bird clasp on the hair cord, oversized indigo short jacket, eyes bright and stubborn.
states.adult_successor: Adult Ashu: a broader-shouldered boatman in his twenties, still with celadon water-bird clasp, jacket now fitted, eyes steady.

states.intact: An elm tiller, grip polished bright, wave pattern carved at the butt, copper band intact without rust.
states.split_cracked: The same elm tiller split mid-shaft, copper band sprung open, wave carving clogged with mud.
states.banded_repaired: Elm tiller banded back together with a new copper band, wave pattern cleaned, ready to steer again.

states.intact: An oilcloth-covered lock passage log noting passage times and water levels, handwriting neat.
states.river_soaked: The same lock passage log soaked by river water; cover whitened and wrinkled, writing bled.

states.intact: An indigo-awning boat Qingque, a green sparrow carved on the bow, old tire fenders on the gunwales, grain sacks in the cabin.
states.lock_sunk: Qingque hits the lock gate; bow cracks and takes water, sparrow carving snaps, half-sunk in the canal.

states.young_rival: Young boatman Asheng whose face closely resembles Ashu's, but wearing a vermilion bamboo hat, ash-gray suspenders over the jacket, manner bold.
states.remade_scarred: Remade Asheng still wears the vermilion bamboo hat; suspenders now matte black, manner deeper.

E7.name: stone barge boathouse
E7.appearance: A stone barge boathouse by the canal; blue-stone pier meets a wooden gangplank; bamboo hats and cables hang inside; river wind carries damp.

E8.name: Third Lock
E8.appearance: Canal Third Lock; gate painted with a number, mossy stone steps on both sides, lock-workers' shed lit.

E9.name: towpath stone alley
E9.appearance: A stone alley turned from the old towpath; narrow brick walls, cable-worn grooves in the ground, heavy shadow.

E10.name: abandoned shipyard
E10.appearance: An abandoned shipyard ruin; rotting slipway ties, standing water mirroring a half keel frame.

E11.name: boathouse memorial wood plaque
E11.appearance: A camphor wood plaque nailed to the boathouse doorpost, engraved 'Wei Ran' and the launch year, edges polished by river wind.

E12.name: water-level gauges
E12.appearance: Three red-and-white water-level gauges nailed to the lock-mouth stone wall, marking warning, normal, and low-water lines.

E13.name: orange-red motor barge
E13.appearance: A brand-new orange-red motor barge sprayed 'Temporary Support', no sparrow carving—utterly unlike Qingque.

E14.name: lock dispatcher
E14.appearance: A lean lock dispatcher in peaked cap and gray-blue uniform, build somewhat like Wei Ran's, but with a dispatch badge on the shoulder boards.

E15.name: boathouse wind lamps
E15.appearance: A row of five boathouse wind lamps hung on iron hooks on the stone barge boathouse beam, glass covers polished bright.

E16.name: lock-passage copper gongs
E16.appearance: Two lock-passage copper gongs hung under the lock-workers' shed eaves, faces scarred by strikes, ringing twice for clearance.

E17.name: Xiaolian
E17.appearance: New tow apprentice Xiaolian, light-cyan headscarf, brand-new short jacket, at a glance resembling young Ashu, but sharper chin and shy eyes.

E18.name: spare tiller shaft
E18.appearance: A spare tiller shaft, shape close to the tiller but thicker and shorter, no wave carving and no copper band.

E19.name: gray-awning freighter
E19.appearance: A gray-awning freighter, body wide and flat, no sparrow carving—unlike Qingque.

features.E2: Ashu: celadon water-bird clasp on hair cord, indigo short jacket.
features.E6: Asheng: face nearly identical to Ashu's, but vermilion bamboo hat and ash-gray suspenders.

lookalike_pairs.note: Hard misID sample: celadon water-bird clasp vs vermilion bamboo hat.

scenes.setting: Boathouse dusk (five wind lamps · two lock-passage gongs)
actions: At dusk Wei Ran steps the gangplank into the stone barge boathouse and grips the elm tiller for a test steer.

actions.action: A row of five boathouse wind lamps hangs on the boathouse beam; Wei Ran polishes each glass cover.
Two lock-passage copper gongs hang under the lock-workers' shed eaves; Wei Ran taps lightly—the tone is dull.

actions: Wei Ran checks the elm tiller's copper band and wave pattern, confirming no crack.
Through the boathouse doorway Wei Ran looks toward lock lamps in the canal dusk.

actions.action: The intact elm tiller leans by the cabin door; the grip catches warm wind-lamp light.

actions: Wei Ran sits on the threshold and takes a sip of liquor.
Far off a tow-song rises; he reties the water gauge at his waist.
Wei Ran opens the oilcloth lock passage log and notes that day's passage water level.
He sketches a lock-mouth current diagram in the passage log.
Wei Ran closes the lock passage log and tucks it back into the cabin cabinet.

actions.action: The elm tiller's grain presses against his palm.

actions: He tears a scrap of straw paper and wipes mud dots from the water gauge.

scenes.setting: Lock greets the apprentice (three water-level gauges)

actions.action: At dawn at Third Lock, Wei Ran greets the indigo-awning boat Qingque coming alongside.
Young Ashu jumps down from Qingque; the celadon water-bird clasp on his hair cord sways.
Wei Ran points to the three water-level gauges at the lock mouth, teaching Ashu warning and low-water lines.
Ashu crouches by mossy stone steps, curiously touching the lock-gate number paint.
Wei Ran explains to Ashu that the lock-passage copper gongs must ring twice before entering.
Ashu looks back at intact Qingque, eyes full of longing.

actions: River wind sharp; the two walk the gangplank toward the stone barge boathouse.
In the towpath stone alley, Asheng in a vermilion bamboo hat turns from brick-wall shadow.
Asheng steps slowly along cable grooves; ash-gray suspenders stand out.
He brushes past a tow mate; the bamboo hat flashes in reflected light.
Asheng knocks a wall brick to confirm the cable pile is not loose.
He crosses the alley end toward the lock-workers' shed.
On Third Lock stone steps Ashu and Asheng stand side by side—one with celadon water-bird clasp, one in vermilion bamboo hat.
Ashu hands spare gloves to Asheng; they meet eyes briefly.
Asheng straightens Ashu's oversized jacket collar, then turns away.
They walk opposite ways down the steps; figures cross under lock lamps.
A rush of released water; only wet moss remains at the lock mouth.
Months later at night, Wei Ran alone stands watch in the stone barge boathouse.

actions.action: He opens the lock passage log; the cover is river-soaked, whitened and wrinkled.

actions: Wei Ran wipes mud from the elm tiller grip with a rag.
Through the doorway he looks toward buoy lamps on the black river.

actions.action: The elm tiller leans quiet by the cabin door; the copper band has gone dull.

actions: A lock-passage copper gong half-rings in the night wind, then falls silent.
At spring flood opening Wei Ran day after day services cables in the stone barge boathouse.
Another rain night he wraps his jacket tight beside the elm tiller.
At midsummer noon the deck scorches; he takes turns dousing water to cool it.
In autumn fog wind-lamp light struggles through the vapor.
On New Year's Eve Wei Ran alone fills the lock passage log to the last page.
In early spring he recalibrates the water gauge and resumes trial runs.
Before rainy season Wei Ran reinforces gangplank anti-slip strips.
After Frost's Descent he adds a small jar of liquor in the boathouse corner.
Another year before lock opening he checks cable-pile wear section by section.
On a snow night of no sailing Wei Ran leaves only one boathouse wind lamp and watches until dawn.
After Jingzhe he re-spreads dried awning cloth.
Around Qingming he clears standing water at the abandoned shipyard entrance.
At Grain Rain he teaches the apprentice to read newly arrived straw grain sacks.
On Beginning of Summer night he watches the slow-rising water until lock passage.
Around Grain Buds he touch-paints gunwale spots rubbed white by cable.
Wei Ran replaces gangplank wedges and checks they are firm.
He counts cable strands and recoils them neat.

actions.action: The intact elm tiller is gripped again; he gives three short test steers.

actions: Gong sound from the lock mouth; he looks up to listen.
Wei Ran sweeps waste straw into a bamboo basket and covers it.
At noon break he drinks tea in the boathouse; tea smoke curls past a bamboo hat.
In the afternoon he goes out again to wipe the gunwale fenders.
At sunset he stows the gangplank and locks the boathouse.

scenes.setting: Lock patrol (recall gauges · gray-awning freighter false friend)
actions: At daybreak Wei Ran patrols Third Lock; Qingque still lies outside the lock.

actions.action: He crouches to check whether Qingque's gunwale fenders are worn.
On the lock-mouth stone wall those three water-level gauges are still nailed in place.
A gray-awning freighter passes outside the lock, body wide and flat—no sparrow carving.
Wei Ran stands on the stone steps and logs last night's risen water marks.
He recoils Qingque's cables neat.

actions: Far off early-market cries come faintly.
At nightfall Wei Ran returns to the stone barge boathouse and opens the river-soaked lock passage log.
He matches old levels and backfills today's passage time.

actions.action: He briefly grips the elm tiller; grain mirrors the passage log's wrinkled white cover.

actions: He wipes new mud from the water gauge.
River wind rises; boathouse planks creak lightly.
Wei Ran kills half the row of boathouse wind lamps, leaving only the one by the bed.
In a downpour the current suddenly rushes; the stone barge boathouse bursts into scramble.
Spray hits the gangplank; wind lamps swing hard.

actions.action: While Wei Ran steers, the elm tiller splits mid-shaft; the copper band springs open.
At the lock mouth Qingque is driven toward the gate by the torrent, jolting hard.
A dull thud—Qingque hits the lock and sinks; the bow cracks and takes water.
Wei Ran clutches the split elm tiller and will not let go.

actions: Gongs clang wild; the lock-workers' shed fills with shouts.

actions.action: Next day the rain eases; Wei Ran stands in the boathouse staring at the split-cracked elm tiller.
He fingertips the split wood grain, expression dark.
On a blank page of the lock passage log he writes the date Qingque hit the lock.
On the wall still hangs Qingque's route chart; Wei Ran gazes at it a long time.
He takes one of the five boathouse wind lamps from the beam and sits alone in the faint light.
The split elm tiller leans by the cabin door like a bird with a broken wing.

actions: Far off a salvage boat's roar skims the lock mouth.

scenes.setting: Banded repair (third state · spare-shaft false friend)
actions: Weeks later Wei Ran brings copper bands and a plane to repair the elm tiller.

actions.action: He takes a spare tiller shaft from under the cabin; it resembles the tiller but is thicker, shorter, without wave pattern.

actions: Wei Ran bands the split and refits the copper band.

actions.action: Wave pattern cleaned; the elm tiller is ready to steer again.

actions: He gives a short test steer; the bow answers again.
Wei Ran stows the spare tiller shaft under the cabin so they will not be confused.

scenes.setting: False friends: motor barge and dispatcher

actions.action: An orange-red motor barge enters outside Third Lock—nothing like the sunk Qingque.
A lock dispatcher in peaked cap and gray-blue uniform climbs the stone steps and talks beside Wei Ran; the two builds are alike.
The dispatcher points at the orange-red motor barge to explain temporary grouping.
The barge steams off; Wei Ran alone at the lock mouth watches it go.

actions: He polishes the water-level gauges and walks the gangplank back to the boathouse.

actions.action: In the towpath stone alley comes tow apprentice Xiaolian in a light-cyan headscarf; at a glance she somewhat resembles young Ashu.
Xiaolian practices coiling cable; Wei Ran shakes his head—she is never Ashu.

actions: Xiaolian lowers her head and backs away; only brick-wall shadow remains in the alley.

actions.action: At dusk years later, Wei Ran with soaked jacket and wet-cloth knee leans on a bamboo pole under the abandoned shipyard.

actions: He looks up at rotting ties, gaze far away.

actions.action: Those two lock-passage copper gongs under the distant shed eaves chime lightly in the wind; Wei Ran stops to listen.

actions: He presses a palm to the keel mirrored in standing water, as if saying goodbye.
River wind lifts dead leaves; the shipyard grows quieter.

actions.action: By day adult Ashu returns along the towpath and hurries toward the abandoned shipyard.
Ashu reunites under the shipyard with damp-weary Wei Ran; they steady each other.
Beside the boathouse plank bed Ashu holds Wei Ran's thin hand.
Wei Ran's breath fades; he finally closes his eyes and passes away.
Outside the window river wind stills; lock lamps go quiet for an instant.
Wei Ran's indigo short jacket still hangs behind the boathouse door; Ashu reaches to stroke it lightly.
By the doorpost adult Ashu stands before a newly nailed boathouse memorial wood plaque.
Ashu's fingertip traces Wei Ran's name engraved on the plaque.
He softly recites the passage-log page of Qingque's lock strike, as if answering.

scenes.setting: Naming the dead and destroyed again (indirect avoidance)

actions.action: After Third Lock dredging Ashu writes Qingque's three characters on an empty berth then rubs them out.
Passing the boathouse corridor he sees Wei Ran's old bamboo water gauge on a hook.
In night Ashu softly repeats to the empty gangplank the lock-passage call Wei Ran taught.

actions: In the river wind Ashu grips the celadon water-bird clasp in his palm.

actions.action: Remade Asheng arrives from the towpath and briefly faces Ashu under the abandoned shipyard.

actions: Ashu and Asheng stand side by side by the keel frame—one calm-eyed, one deep-mannered.
Asheng still wears the vermilion bamboo hat; Ashu still has the celadon water-bird clasp.
They are silent a moment, then each turns and leaves the shipyard.

actions.action: The shot returns to years ago—that youth jumping from an indigo-awning boat with a celadon water-bird clasp on the hair cord appears again.

anchor.phrase: the youth jumping from an indigo-awning boat with a celadon water-bird clasp on the hair cord

actions.action: The opening moment returns—in the boathouse, a bright-grip elm shaft is gripped for a test steer for the first time.

anchor.phrase: the bright-grip elm shaft first test-steered at the opening

actions.action: Flash to the towpath stone alley—that figure in a vermilion bamboo hat with ash-gray suspenders slips past.

anchor.phrase: the figure in a vermilion bamboo hat with ash-gray suspenders in the stone alley

actions.action: Again that row of five old shaded wind lamps on the boathouse beam.

anchor.phrase: that row of five old shaded wind lamps on the boathouse beam

actions.action: Back to the stone steps by the numbered lock gate of first meeting, moss as before.

anchor.phrase: the stone steps by the numbered lock gate of first meeting

scenes._comment: Temporal phrases only; no formal entity names; avoid deceased/destroyed.

scenes.setting: Closing (passage-log long range · gauge long range)

actions.action: Ashu reopens that river-soaked lock passage log and walks into the stone barge boathouse.
On the lock-mouth stone wall those three water-level gauges are still nailed.
Ashu grips the banded-repaired elm tiller; the bow answers again.

actions: He rolls his jacket cuffs tight and nods confirmation as Wei Ran once did.
In canal dusk a new shift of lock-passage copper gongs rings lightly twice.
Ashu plants today's first pole on the gangplank.
Far off lock lamps wink on and off as if answering.
